$comment: Ported from mlorentedev/dotfiles harness/reviewer-pool.json at 6d92b561 (TOOL-082, #1843;
ADR-070 adopts dotfiles' ADR-046). Unqualified issue numbers below are this repository's;
the dotfiles ones are written mlorentedev/dotfiles#N. The two copies are kept in step by
hand until TOOL-117 (#2295) gives both repositories one source.
kubelab history: this file was the adversarial pool alone (HARNESS-071, #955) and held
the rule that no Anthropic model ever reviews here. ADR-070 replaces that rule with
amendment B below. #1561 (no member declared its credential) is closed by the
secret_id/auth fields every entry now carries; tests/test_reviewer_pool.py holds them.
Reviewer pool for /adversarial-review (HARNESS-071, mlorentedev/dotfiles#955).
Ordered allow-list of models permitted to SIGN a review.md. Since HARNESS-093 the
launcher DRAWS one member at random; the whole array is the gate's allow-list, which
dotf spec archive enforces via checkReviewGate.
Standing rule (amended 2026-10-09, mlorentedev/dotfiles#1923, amendment B): an Anthropic model never
signs an adversarial review ALONE. The reviewer must not be the implementer, and
Claude implements nearly every change in this repo and in dotfiles — BUG-074 was reviewed twice
by claude-opus-5 before anyone noticed, which is the incident this file exists to
prevent. So every signed review keeps a first signature from another vendor, and
an Anthropic member signs only as `signs: second` (a second signature beside a
first signer of another vendor) or `signs: fallback` (in place of the first
signers when they failed for a classified reason the launch request records).
`dotf spec archive` enforces it: pool loading refuses an Anthropic member that
would sign first, and the gate checks roles, reason and that the vendors differ.
Second signature: required when proposal.md declares `risk: high`. Only Sonnet
declares `signs: second` today, so a high-risk spec's second signature depends on
the Anthropic review key; when it is down, wait, or waive or lower the risk in
proposal.md with a stated reason. That dependency is deliberate (the owner wants
the quality tier in play, 2026-10-09) and costs about 8 reviews a month.
`vendor` is who trains the model: the unit the second signature must differ in.
`signs` defaults to `first`.
PR-Agent reads this file too (AI-045 AC9, mlorentedev/dotfiles#1923): each `pr_agent` block is that
member's PR-Agent model, its weight in the CI draw, and its reasoning effort.
`route: risk` is not drawn: it reviews first when a PR crosses `pr_agent_risk`
(changed lines, or the label). scripts/pr-agent-route.sh holds the allowlist of
Anthropic models CI may spend on, so an edit here cannot route CI onto another.
kubelab only (owner decision 2026-10-18, #1957): each NaN member's `pr_agent` block carries a
`forge_rank`, the order in which the forge's own reviewer (deploy/pr-agent) tries its models.
That server cannot draw per review as CI does, so it needs an order, and `weight` is not one:
it is a spending share, and it put mimo-v2.6-flash first, the model whose long reasoning is
most often cut at about 600 s (lesson-601). `forge_rank` puts the fast model first (deepseek,
then glm, then mimo). CI never reads it and no weight moved for it. dotfiles' copy has no such
key: when re-porting this file, keep it, and tests/test_pr_agent_config_render.py will say so
if it is lost. The consumers ignore unknown keys (dotf's reader is a plain json decode,
scripts/pr-agent-route.sh selects fields with jq).
Entries are model IDS, not tool names, and that distinction is load-bearing:
`agy` also serves claude-opus-4-6-thinking and claude-sonnet-4-6, so pinning
the tool would guarantee nothing. Pinning the id does.
`id` is the canonical string a reviewer records in review.md and the gate
matches on. `provider`/`model` are the launcher's flags, kept explicit rather
than parsed out of `id`: BUG-074 round 3 ran on the right model only because
~/.pi/agent/settings.json on one machine happened to default to it — pi's own
default provider is google, and that file is unversioned per-machine state.
A pin that depends on a default is not a pin.
Reasoning-class only. The latency-optimised daily models (nan/qwen3.6,
nan/gemma4) are deliberately absent: a reviewer that PASSes cheaply is worse
than no gate, because it converts the gate into a green checkmark. This file
is read once per spec, so slow is fine. A member is admitted by the bar, not
by its tier name: gemini-3.8-flash-high is in because agy dropped its Pro tier
and Flash at High effort found the planted defect (owner decision 2026-10-14,
mlorentedev/dotfiles#2385). gpt-oss-120b-medium is out because it missed it twice; never admit it.
This is the load-bearing slice of H-044, not a replacement for it. H-044's
model-map.json maps a neutral tier (top|mid|low) to a provider per agent — a
different shape. Kept in a separate file so H-044 need not migrate this one.

Order is provenance, not precedence, since HARNESS-093 (mlorentedev/dotfiles#1370): the launcher draws one first-signer member at random (an Anthropic member is never drawn first), so every first signer is exercised in the ordinary course of reviews and NaN's per-model concurrency buckets are spread; --reviewer names one deliberately, which is how a run is reproduced. The roles below record why each member was admitted, not who runs first.

On saturation, measured 2026-08-20: NaN's concurrency limit is PER MODEL, not per API key (8 concurrent to deepseek gives 5x200 + 3x429, while mimo answers 200 during that saturation). So a spec review launched while the PR reviewer is saturating deepseek WILL fail, and falling through to another entry is the correct response rather than a bug. Do not 'fix' that by promoting the NaN sibling above the provider-diverse entry — it would trade an outage-proof fallback for a saturation-proof one and lose the stronger property. This file is read once per spec, so slow is fine; that is why availability does not outrank independence here.

pool.why: 1M context and a mandatory reasoning chain — roughly 4x slower than qwen3.6 on trivial prompts, which is the correct trade for a gate that runs once per spec. Exercised: BUG-074 round 3 re-ran the mutation battery itself rather than trusting the spec's table. kubelab, 2026-08-21 (#1205): under PR-Agent this model returned a 200 with an EMPTY body, spending its output on reasoning (4m15s of silence on #1202, run 32440498259), the same shape as the 32768-token completion cap NaN applies when no max_tokens is sent (#1957, lesson-601). The forge reviewer now sends max_tokens 65536 (#2479) and tries this model first (forge_rank 1); CI's draw is unchanged.

A second provider family, independent of both NaN and Anthropic — provider diversity rather than merely a different model. Flash tier at high effort, admitted 2026-10-14 by owner decision (mlorentedev/dotfiles#2385) when agy stopped serving gemini-3.1-pro-high, the id this arm held until then, so roughly one random draw in five died at startup. Admitted on the bar every member clears: the planted `((count++))` defect under `set -e` with count=0 (agy 1.3.5, macOS). It found the defect in 54 s, named a failing input and gave the fix. gpt-oss-120b-medium, the only other non-Anthropic id agy serves, missed it twice and must not be admitted. PROVISIONAL: when Gemini ships new models, measure them on the same bar and replace this one if one passes. agy has no --provider flag; the model id selects the family. AUTH IS LOGIN, not a key (mlorentedev/dotfiles#1156): agy holds an OAuth token at ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/google_credentials.json and answers with no API key in the environment at all (measured 2026-08-22). This entry previously named GEMINI_API_KEY, a secret the registry has never declared, so every attempt to use the provider-diverse arm died at `dotf secrets run --only` -- and nothing noticed, because the primary always answered. The arm this pool exists to provide had therefore never run once.

Re-admitted 2026-09-30 on the bar this file requires, not renamed in. NaN retired its predecessor mimo-v2.5 that day: it hung, then answered 401 'This API key does not have access to the requested model' (AI-045, mlorentedev/dotfiles#1763). mimo-v2.5 had been admitted 2026-08-20 on a planted-defect test, and the successor was given the same one: the `((count++))` exit-status-1 case under `set -e` from this repo's prohibited-pattern table. mimo-v2.6-flash found it in 21 s and 772 completion tokens, named a failing input (count=0), and gave the fix (`count=$((count + 1))`). deepseek-v4-flash, run on the same prompt, found the same defect in 9 s. That is agreement on one planted defect, not a quality ranking, and it is stated as that. It stays a SECOND fallback, after the provider-diverse one, because provider diversity remains the stronger property. Profile: 1M context, reasoning chain, which is this pool's line against qwen3.6 and gemma4 at 262K.
pool.operational_note: Reasoning models here emit reasoning_content BEFORE content. Under-provisioning max_tokens returns an empty body with finish_reason=length and no error — the same shape as a review that silently did not happen (lesson 213). Provision generously and check finish_reason. NaN recommends max_tokens >= 300 for this model and publishes a per-model concurrency limit of 5.

pool.why: Admitted 2026-08-29 by owner decision (HARNESS-093, mlorentedev/dotfiles#1370) to spread reviews across NaN's PER-MODEL concurrency buckets and exercise more than one model on the gate. What IS established: reasoning-class by profile — pi-nan-provider's snapshot marks glm5.3-flash reasoning: true with a 1M context, the line this pool draws (dotfiles tests/pi-nan-package.bats holds it). What is NOT established: a calibration against a review of known outcome (e.g. CLI-050 round 1's real Major); recorded here so nobody reads this entry as measured equivalence to deepseek. Drawn at random like every member; --reviewer names it deliberately.

Admitted 2026-08-29 by owner decision (HARNESS-093, mlorentedev/dotfiles#1370) to spread reviews across NaN's per-model concurrency buckets and exercise more than one model on the gate. What IS established: reasoning-class by profile — pi-nan-provider's snapshot marks qwen3.8-flash reasoning: true, and dotfiles ai/pi/models.json corrects its stale native-window snapshot to NaN's served 1,048,576-token window (dotfiles tests/pi-nan-package.bats holds the effective values). What is NOT established: a calibration against a review of known outcome (e.g. CLI-050 round 1's real Major); recorded here so nobody reads this entry as measured equivalence to deepseek. Drawn at random like every member; --reviewer names it deliberately.

Admitted 2026-10-09 by owner decision (mlorentedev/dotfiles#1923, amendment B). In the adversarial review it signs only as a FALLBACK, with a classified reason (rate limit, quota, provider error, timeout, content filter, empty answer) when the NaN first signers failed; it never signs first by draw. In PR-Agent it is drawn at weight 35, about a third of reviews, because NaN's shared per-model concurrency is the scarcer resource and the owner judged the spend acceptable (2026-10-14, mlorentedev/dotfiles#2215). Measured on four real reviews (25K-55K tokens in, 9K-32K out, all under the 100K price step): about $0.02-0.06 a review, 3 to 7 times the $0.008 this entry first estimated, because thinking tokens bill as output. Reasoning-class by profile (adaptive thinking). Effort is medium, not high: at high, thinking spent the 32,000-token output cap on large diffs and the answer came back empty in 5 of 11 runs (mlorentedev/dotfiles#2458). No calibration against a review of known outcome yet; mlorentedev/dotfiles#2215 and mlorentedev/dotfiles#2216 measure its addressed-comment rate.

Admitted 2026-10-09 by owner decision (mlorentedev/dotfiles#1923, amendment B) as the quality tier, placed where it pays: the SECOND signature of a `risk: high` spec (about 8 a month, about $1.60 each agentic), and in PR-Agent the first review of a PR past `pr_agent_risk` (about 3% of PRs at 1500 changed lines, about $0.37 each, measured). Never drawn at random in either flow: at 15x Haiku's PR-Agent price a uniform share would spend the month's budget in a week. No calibration yet; mlorentedev/dotfiles#2215 and mlorentedev/dotfiles#2216 measure it.

pr_agent_risk.label: deep-review
pr_agent_risk.$comment: A PR reviews first on the `route: risk` member when its additions plus deletions reach min_changed_lines, or it carries the label. Set to 1500 by owner decision 2026-10-09: the first live Sonnet review cost $0.37, not $0.13, because a PR this large fills the prompt cap, and over the last 395 merged PRs 9.1% reach 900 lines, 4.8% reach 1200 and 3.0% reach 1500. At 1500 the route costs about $28 of the $60-65 month. A path-based predicate matched 14-35% and was rejected as too costly. Recalibrate at mlorentedev/dotfiles#2215 / mlorentedev/dotfiles#2216.
